gen-fredoka-general-sans: Fredoka holds a single pen width from stem to curve. The heading is the approachable voice up top, while General Sans, a sans with a lowercase that fills the line, slides smoothly around every bend.
gen-fredoka-gf-graduate: Soft and bookish at once: Fredoka's single-width line meets Graduate, a serif with generous space between its letters. Friendly openness up top, and a dignified, spaced-out serif settling in beneath.
gen-fredoka-gf-lisu-bosa: Friendly up top, sturdy below. Fredoka keeps a single pen width and an open e, while Lisu Bosa adds sturdy, large-looking words with a lightly flexed stroke beneath it.
gen-fredoka-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana: Fredoka keeps a friendly single-width line and an open e. Noto Serif Hentaigana, a serif with open jaws on every curved stroke and small letters nearly as tall as capitals, is where the real difference lives.
gen-fs-alpino-fs-erode: Felt-tip friendly, Alpino stands tall and generous in every weight. Erode, with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb of stroke weight, keeps paragraphs moving with dignified, unhurried ease.
gen-fs-array-fs-ranade: Ranade reads loose and spread-out, its stroke ends far apart. Array, futuristic and precise, brings large lowercase eyes up top, and the pairing feels made for quick visits rather than marathons.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-fs-karma: Azeret Mono sets every letter in a fixed-width, code-style slot. Karma, a serif with a mild taper and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, lets text glide along without snagging the eye.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-fs-public-sans: Technical and functional, Azeret Mono spaces its fixed-width letters generously. Public Sans, a sans with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, fills in the body while the monospace heading stays crisp up top.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-fs-ranade: Azeret Mono lays out fixed-width, code-style letters with generous tracking that opens each word. Ranade, with slightly shifting weight and widely spaced type, then loosens the body text to match.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-instrument-sans: Azeret Mono locks its code-style letters into fixed-width slots, with generous tracking between them. And Instrument Sans, with one unvarying stroke weight and a minimal step from capitals to lowercase, moves along smoothly beneath.
